correctness.rationale: The fixed named equivalence relations are precisely equality of the two coordinates. A single deletion creates a unique deficient E-class and F-class, detected by the explicit 3-variable empty-intersection predicate; all full grids lack it. At width 2, a permanent back-and-forth preserves all four possible two-element relation types, with singleton-class exceptions exactly in deficient dimensions of size two. Width k>=3 recovers ordinary coordinate counts up to k using local variable shadowing, and a permanent coordinate-index k-pebble invariant proves the converse and sharpness at unrestricted depth. Finite independent verification checks succeeded, but serve only as corroboration.

value.rationale: The single-hole erasure stability boundary is a natural logical expressiveness question for two transverse equivalences. The theorem simultaneously supplies a sharp width-2/width-3 transition, all higher variable-width cutoffs, all exceptional phases, exact theory counts, unique minimum-size representatives and strictness witnesses. The results are a complete structural classification rather than routine finite enumeration.
